items.title_orig: Thursday night Goodwill haul. Excited for The Temper Trap & The Magnetic Fields!
"Grunge and Stoner Rock picked up where heavy metal left off in 1976." - Jack Endino
items.article_text:
To be specific, I heard Endino (famous rock producer and member of Skin Yard) basically make this same statement in a documentary about grunge and one about stoner rock, and I think it's an interesting concept. He said grunge and stoner rock were picking up where heavy metal left off in 1976, with some punk ethos and a respect for noise. I think to some degree you can probably extend this to doom in general, and to some extent even to sludge.
 Obviously it isn't strictly true - we know Cobain liked Metallica's Ride the Lightning, that the Pearl Jam guys liked Venom, and that early extreme metal acts like Celtic Frost were hugely influential in modern doom metal.
